runs.content:
**Investigation idea:** Games Workshop (GAW) — a live +300%-gain pension holding — has no Finance idea page despite today's new Burry research specifically flagging it as needing a hedge. finance/michael-burry/burry-options-approach.md's "Pension Portfolio — Hedging Candidates" table lists GAW for a collar strategy specifically because of its outsized unrealised gain, but finance/portfolio-overview.md is the only place GAW appears in the wiki at all — no dedicated idea-gaw.md, no verdict, no risk discussion of what happens if Warhammer licensing revenue decelerates. Every other position in that same hedging table (AVGO, GOOGL, CHIP) has extensive supporting research elsewhere in the wiki; GAW has none. Next step: run /equity-analyst GAW.L (or a manual short write-up) now that a specific, dated trigger (the hedging recommendation) exists.

**Cross-domain connection 1:** Fred's real pension portfolio holds a +300%-gain equity stake in one of the world's most successful games companies, and the Games domain has never referenced it. finance/portfolio-overview.md carries Games Workshop (GAW.L) as a live holding, entered at 5,045p and now 20,200p (~+300%), with its own Thesis Status row describing the business as "Warhammer IP licensing + direct sales; high-margin royalty model." Today's newly-created finance/michael-burry/burry-options-approach.md treats that exact gain as a live hedging candidate via a collar. Yet games/overview.md and games/prototypes.md — the domain built around Fred's own AI-assisted game prototyping — make zero mention of GAW, despite it being the single most successful "games business" anywhere in his own portfolio. Next step: cross-link games/overview.md to portfolio-overview.md's GAW position as a real-world proof point for high-margin IP licensing.

**Cross-domain connection 2:** Today's newest Finance research page documents a rival to the Kelly Criterion that Sports Betting's own bankroll stub has never considered. finance/michael-burry/burry-options-approach.md (created today) states Burry "doesn't appear to use formal Kelly sizing for options" — instead using a patience/conviction/time-horizon approach ("the more patience, the larger a position can be"). sports-betting/bankroll-management.md's own "Key Concepts (to be built out)" list still treats Kelly/fractional Kelly as the only sizing framework worth building out, and still hasn't ported over finance/concepts/concept-kelly-criterion.md (flagged 2026-07-11, still open). This adds a new angle: Finance's own most-documented real-money bettor explicitly rejects formal Kelly sizing in favour of a named alternative Sports Betting doesn't know exists yet. Next step: once the Kelly page is ported over, add a short "alternative: patience-based sizing (Burry)" note alongside it.

Friday focus (Lightfin + Games + Cooking + Sports Betting + Work): deep-read the overview/index pages for all five domains plus recent Cooking recipe-suggestions batches; log.md since the last thinker run (2026-07-30) showed no new ingestion in those five domains — the only fresh material was Finance's new options-trading research (concept-options-trading.md, burry-options-approach.md, /options-trade-recommender skill) and a Cooking recipe-recommender batch. Both new findings came from checking that fresh Finance material against today's focus domains (Games, Sports Betting) rather than new source ingestion in the focus domains themselves.

**Investigation idea:** Books' own July recommender named the exact book that would supply the fraud-analysis lens Crypto's own worst holdings need, and it's sitting unread. books/suggestions.md's July 2026 batch recommends *Number Go Up* (Zeke Faux) specifically because it "chases crypto fraud from Sam Bankman-Fried to a Cambodian scam compound — same fraud-detective energy as Red Notice and his short-selling research, aimed at his live crypto portfolio." That's not a generic pitch — it's naming the precise gap the wiki already flagged on 2026-07-05/07-06 (Finance's Hindenburg-style red-flags checklist in finance/short-research/concept-short-selling.md has never been run against Fred's own $LUCKY/$TEST holdings in Crypto portfolio.md, both CertiK 3.5/10 with −90%/−98% drawdowns from ATH, no thesis or continued-hold rationale in either Notes row). The book isn't on books/reading-list.md yet, so this connection currently only exists inside the recommendation's own "Why Fred" text — nobody has acted on it. Next step: add Number Go Up to reading-list.md's aspirational section now (don't wait for the Aug 1 book-summarizer cycle), cross-linked to concept-short-selling.md and a note on Crypto portfolio.md's $LUCKY/$TEST rows once read.

**Cross-domain connection:** Today's podcast recommendation is a dedicated clinical-research show on the exact dementia-prevention mechanism Health's own source page documents, and it lands one day after Games got linked to the same research for the opposite reason. podcasts/suggestions.md's week-of-2026-07-30 batch recommends Dementia Matters (Dr. Nathaniel Chin, University of Wisconsin Alzheimer's Disease Research Center) explicitly for covering "modifiable risk factors" and current Alzheimer's prevention trials — narrower and more clinically specific than the longevity-generalist shows already suggested (Attia, Health Longevity Secrets). health/source-wood-brain-sharp-2026.md is the wiki's own existing primary source on exactly this: the 14 Lancet modifiable risk factors, the "45%+ of dementia cases may be preventable" headline, and a dedicated Cognitive Stimulation section. Neither page references the other. Distinct from yesterday's connection (Health's research naming game-building as protective, unlinked from Games) — that one was about an existing source being under-used inside the wiki; this one is about a brand-new external show that could directly extend the same source once listened to. Next step: if Fred picks up Dementia Matters, use it to expand source-wood-brain-sharp-2026.md's Cognitive Stimulation section with newer clinical detail, cross-linked back to the podcast suggestion.

Thursday focus (Books + Podcasts): deep-read Books - overview.md, books/reading-list.md, books/suggestions.md, Podcasts - overview.md, and podcasts/suggestions.md (all weeks, including today's fresh 2026-07-30 batch), cross-checked memory/index.md's Domain Content Status and Open Threads, and reviewed log.md since the last thinker run (2026-07-29) — the only new activity was today's podcast-recommender run (4 shows: Dividend Talk, Unchained, Dementia Matters, The Cognitive Revolution). Both findings above came from checking today's fresh recommendation batch and the existing July book-suggestion batch against the rest of the wiki's already-logged gaps, rather than new source ingestion.
